--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective." / "The general advice says: 'A conciliatory action can sometimes help end a chain of alternating retaliation. Prefer repairs that support recovering mutual cooperation after a short conflict. A short punishment followed by renewed cooperation may restore coordination.'"
STRATEGY: Parent is a cooperative TFT-like strategy that mostly cooperates, punishes defection, and probes late. The trace simulates the 12 source opponents and designs an adaptive strategy that starts with D to test retaliation, exploits always-C opponents, then repairs to cooperation. It changes the parent by adding early defection testing, opponent classification, and final-round exploitation.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says: 'A conciliatory action can sometimes help end a chain of alternating retaliation. Prefer repairs that support recovering mutual cooperation after a short conflict. A short punishment followed by renewed cooperation may restore coordination.'"
STRATEGY: Parent is a tournament strategy that exploits non-retaliators by defecting while the opponent cooperates, then repairs after a defection. The trace simulates this two-phase exploit/cooperative-repair design against opponents like always-C, TFT, and slot 8. It revises the repair protocol (e.g., forgiving TFT, probe length, spaced probes) to reduce the cost of the defection spiral.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, the proposed strategy seems solid and likely improves over parent."
STRATEGY: The parent is a cooperative/TFT-style strategy with repair and final-round defection. The trace simulates a new "exploit while opponent never defects, then repair and TFT" strategy against the 12 opponents. It changes the opening to D, adds an exploit phase, a 3-round repair phase after first opponent D, a high-defection fallback, and final-round D.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Overall, this strategy is simple and should perform well. It exploits non-retaliators heavily, and is forgiving to retaliators. It should improve over parent which did not exploit always C and had complex heuristics."
STRATEGY: Parent used rng and complex heuristics, did not always exploit an always-C opponent. Simulated the new deterministic strategy against always-C, slot 5 exploitative, TFT, and always-D opponents. Changed to defect first, exploit while opponent never defects, defect on last round, defect if opponent defected every round or >70% after round 10, cooperate for 3 rounds after first opponent defection, then TFT.
